kis.title: Google Research ASPEST: Bridging Active Sample Acquisition & Selective Prediction via Checkpoint Ensembles

claims.assertion: active_selective_prediction evaluates active adaptation and selective abstention across six domain-shift benchmarks (mnist->svhn, cifar10->cinic10, fmow, amazon_review, domainnet, otto).

ASPEST maintains a checkpoint ensemble (update_ensemble_state), queries bounded label budgets via AverageMarginSampling over test shifts, self-trains with KL-divergence only on samples within a gated confidence band [lower_threshold, upper_threshold), and scores abstention from max ensemble probability.

kis.distilled_learning: Combine low-budget human oracle labeling (average-margin sampling) with dual-thresholded KL self-training over running checkpoint ensembles so selective prediction abstention thresholds stay calibrated under target distribution shift.

kis.title: Google Research CISC: Confidence-Informed Self-Consistency & Within-Question Discrimination (WQD)

claims.assertion: CISC extracts per-trace confidence via ConfidenceExtractionConfig (temperature=0.0, num_tokens=10, verbal_eos_pattern=')') and ConfidenceExtractionType variants (NONE, BINARY, BINARY_FT, BINARY_FT01, BINARY_MP, HUNDRED), bundled in AggregatedConfidenceExtractionConfig across verbal_confidence, confidence_likelihoods, and run_sequence_probability.

majority_with_conf() implements confidence-weighted self-consistency voting supporting NormalizationType (NONE, LINEAR, SOFTMAX), frozen AggregatorConfig validation across four confidence column families, zero-confidence retention while filtering NaN/empty entries, tie-break-only mode, and normalized chosen-answer confidence output.

calculate_metrics_at_position() produces frozen ResultMetrics quantifying comparable_baseline_traces_needed vs standard SC (>40% path reduction across 9 models and 4 datasets per cisc/README.md), paired with calibration_util.py (compute_ece, compute_brier, TemperatureScaling) and WQD discrimination analysis over ECE.

kis.distilled_learning: Replace unweighted self-consistency majority voting with temperature-normalized confidence-weighted voting (CISC majority_with_conf + SOFTMAX/LINEAR normalization) and evaluate selection quality via Within-Question Discrimination (WQD) rather than global calibration (ECE) alone.

kis.title: Google Research UQ Benchmark 2019: Predictive Uncertainty Under Dataset Shift, Brier Decomposition & Confidence-Threshold Coverage

claims.assertion: uq_benchmark_2019 benchmarks Vanilla, Temperature Scaling, Deep Ensemble, MC Dropout, SVI, and Last-Layer variants under dataset shift (MNIST-rot, CIFAR-10-C, ImageNet-C, Criteo-corrupt, 20 Newsgroups/LM1B), showing post-hoc temperature scaling falls short under shift relative to model marginalization/ensembles.

metrics_lib.py implements expected_calibration_error(), expected_calibration_error_multiclass(), compute_accuracies_at_confidences() threshold-coverage sweeps, brier_decomposition() into uncertainty/resolution/reliability, and quantile binning with 0->1e-8 guard for np.digitize.

calibration_lib.py fits maximum-likelihood temperature via scipy.optimize.bisect over TF Categorical/Bernoulli NLL gradients in find_scaling_temperature() and applies it via apply_temperature_scaling().

kis.distilled_learning: Evaluate predictive uncertainty under distribution shift using confidence-threshold selectivity sweeps (compute_accuracies_at_confidences) and Brier uncertainty/resolution/reliability decomposition rather than trusting in-distribution temperature scaling alone.
